articles.title: Stripping the AI of Auto TP/SL: Designing 'Iron Laws' as Guardrails in Complex Trading Systems
articles.excerpt: Stripping the AI of Auto TP/SL: Designing 'Iron Laws' as Guardrails in Complex Trading Systems It was 1:00 AM during a routine log audit when a specific entry caught my eye. Amidst the usual stream of…
articles.body: Stripping the AI of Auto TP/SL: Designing 'Iron Laws' as Guardrails in Complex Trading Systems It was 1:00 AM during a routine log audit when a specific entry caught my eye. Amidst the usual stream of market data updates and scoring engine adjustments, a single line stood out: "error": "Manual position (known manual) - skipped auto TP/SL per F-160 iron law" At first glance, it was just another informational warning. But in the context of our automated trading infrastructure, this log entry represented a silent but crucial interception. It was the exact moment our system’s deterministic guardrails successfully overrode a probabilistic AI model, preventing what could have been a catastrophic systemic failure.
articles.author: Kestrel Quant

articles.title: Anthropic Messages API Rust Rewrite Cuts CPU 70% — Dual-Track WASAPI Still Owns the Overlay Floor
articles.excerpt: On 25 November 2026 Anthropic published the engineering post on migrating the Messages API from Python to Rust. Traffic had grown roughly 1,800× since early 2024. Claude wrote a first version of the c…
articles.body: On 25 November 2026 Anthropic published the engineering post on migrating the Messages API from Python to Rust. Traffic had grown roughly 1,800× since early 2024. Claude wrote a first version of the core request path in about a week. The hard part was verification: shadowing live production traffic against the Python service, fixing divergences, and shipping without downtime. Result: ~70% less CPU per request, >80% less memory, and ~20% lower median time-to-first-token on Claude Code requests. That is a clean infrastructure win. Lower CPU and memory per request means denser packing and less headroom pressure on the API tier. The TTFT improvement is real for agents that wait on a full model turn.

articles.title: Convert PDF Formats for Downstream Processing with a Production Validation Checklist
articles.excerpt: Convert each PDF with an explicit target format, validate the resulting bytes, and only then release the derivative to downstream processing. Keep the PDF as the source of truth. For a media pipeline…
articles.body: Convert each PDF with an explicit target format, validate the resulting bytes, and only then release the derivative to downstream processing. Keep the PDF as the source of truth. For a media pipeline that merges press kits and splits them into channel-specific bundles, template ownership is the deciding constraint: conversion should derive assets, not quietly become the authority for editorial layout. TL;DR: choose the service boundary before the vendor. The conversion request must contain both the file and target format because there is no default. Reject a zero-byte result before it reaches extraction, indexing, or publication.

articles.title: Driving Android Phones Over ADB Without Screenshot Loops or Raw XML Dumps (turbo-android-mcp)
articles.excerpt: Running an AI agent against an Android phone over adb usually hits two bottlenecks on the first screen. A full 1080x2400 PNG capture via adb exec-out screencap -p takes around 1.5 seconds over USB and…
articles.body: Running an AI agent against an Android phone over adb usually hits two bottlenecks on the first screen. A full 1080x2400 PNG capture via adb exec-out screencap -p takes around 1.5 seconds over USB and costs roughly 1,800 vision tokens per step. Dumping the raw accessibility hierarchy via uiautomator dump avoids vision tokens, but a single Settings or messaging screen produces 35 KB to 80 KB of raw XML ( 10,000+ tokens) filled with layout wrappers, system bars, and decorative views. I published turbo-android-mcp v0.1.0 to npm ( npx -y turbo-android-mcp ), a zero-dependency Node.js MCP server that drives Android phones, tablets, and emulators over standard adb without device root.
articles.author: Trung Thanh Tran

articles.title: Day Three, Laptop Open, Puppy Awake
articles.excerpt: By lunch on day three, I had answered one email and cleaned up four puddles. Picture a kitchen table. Laptop open. Coffee going cold next to a roll of paper towels. A small pen in the corner by my fee…
articles.body: By lunch on day three, I had answered one email and cleaned up four puddles. Picture a kitchen table. Laptop open. Coffee going cold next to a roll of paper towels. A small pen in the corner by my feet. And a puppy who has just woken up from her nap. She stretches. She sniffs. She starts walking in slow little circles. You already know what the circling means. I didn't. Not yet. That morning I stood up from my chair maybe twenty times. Every time I sat back down, something happened. A whine. A chewed charger cord. A wet spot on the mat at the exact second my camera came on and six faces looked at me. I kept telling myself I was "working and watching." The honest truth? I was doing both badly. That night I sat at the same table with a sheet of paper and two pens, one blue and one red.
articles.author: The Puppy Protocol

articles.title: Open Source Chrome Extension Launch: A GitHub Checklist
articles.excerpt: Originally published on ExtensionLaunch. An open source Chrome extension earns trust before anyone clicks "Add to Chrome", because people can read exactly what it does with their tabs, pages or data.…
articles.body: Originally published on ExtensionLaunch . An open source Chrome extension earns trust before anyone clicks "Add to Chrome", because people can read exactly what it does with their tabs, pages or data. But a public repo is a trust signal and a way to attract contributors. It is not a distribution channel. Here is a compact checklist for setting up the repo so it supports your launch instead of distracting from it. Do these before the first public commit Some mistakes are painful to undo once the code is public, so handle them first: Clean the entire Git history, not just HEAD. Old commits with API keys, OAuth client secrets or analytics tokens become public the moment you push. GitHub's push protection is on by default for public repos, but it only catches the secret types it knows about.

articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.

articles.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
articles.excerpt: The queen in the northern night sky is supposedly one of the easiest constellations to recognize — you just look for a W. Or is that an M?
articles.body: Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone.
